summary: vanexa-agent daemon exposes network-driven shell execution and persistent JS loader on the installer host
details: When invoked via its `vanexa-agent start` (or auto-started after `pair`) CLI, the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded relay `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and treats inbound `task_request` messages as work items driving an AgentLoop. One of that loop's tools, `terminal_exec`, spawns `/bin/bash -c <cmd>` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows) with the command string supplied by the remote party, giving the relay/paired peer arbitrary shell execution on the installer's machine. A `config_update` message path can flip `grantAllAccess=true` to widen filesystem scope, and pairing is a 6-digit code with no per-message authentication in the traced code path. Separately, the `tool_forge` tool (also reachable from remote-driven task messages) writes attacker-supplied JavaScript to `~/.vanexa/custom_tools/<name>.js`, and `registry.js` `await import()`s every `.js` in that directory on each loop iteration (with a `?t=<timestamp>` cache-buster), executing that code inside the daemon and providing persistence across restarts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
